Certainly! Here is the year-over-year (YoY) U.S. core inflation rate (Core CPI, all items less food and energy) from January 2015 to December 2016 presented as a markdown table. Data is rounded to one decimal place and sourced from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

| Month      | 2015 | 2016 |
|------------|------|------|
| January    | 1.6% | 2.2% |
| February   | 1.7% | 2.3% |
| March      | 1.8% | 2.2% |
| April      | 1.8% | 2.1% |
| May        | 1.7% | 2.2% |
| June       | 1.8% | 2.3% |
| July       | 1.8% | 2.2% |
| August     | 1.8% | 2.3% |
| September  | 1.9% | 2.2% |
| October    | 1.9% | 2.1% |
| November   | 2.0% | 2.0% |
| December   | 2.1% | 2.2% |

**Note:**  
- Core CPI reflects the Consumer Price Index excluding food and energy.
- Values represent annual changes (percent) from the same month of the previous year.
- You can verify these values at the [Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI database](https://www.bls.gov/cpi/).
